title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is a process used by plants, algae and some bacteria to convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

title: Printing press
text: The movable-type printing press, introduced to Europe by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, made books cheap enough to spread literacy and ideas across the continent.

title: Tide
text: Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun and the rotation of the Earth.

title: Binary search
text: Binary search finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search interval, taking O(log n) comparisons.

title: Vaccination
text: Vaccination trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen by exposing it to a harmless form of the agent, so later infection is milder or prevented.

title: Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across northern China over many centuries to protect against invasions.

title: Plate tectonics
text: Plate tectonics describes the slow movement of Earth's lithospheric plates, which causes earthquakes, volcanoes and the formation of mountain ranges.

title: Coffee
text: Coffee is a brewed drink prepared from roasted coffee beans, the seeds of berries from Coffea plants, and is one of the most widely consumed beverages in the world.

title: Transistor
text: The transistor, invented at Bell Labs in 1947, is a semiconductor device that amplifies or switches electronic signals and underpins all modern computing.

title: Monarch butterfly
text: Monarch butterflies undertake a multi-generational migration of thousands of kilometres between North America and overwintering sites in Mexico.
